title: Refactor sync-ai-rules.sh into maintainable modules
description:
sync-ai-rules.sh has ballooned to well over 1,200 lines of tightly coupled bash covering detection, templating, and per-tool output. The monolithic structure makes it risky to add new capabilities (Codex output, Cursor integration, multi-tool installers), and the lack of unitized helpers leaves repeated logic for file copying, metadata assembly, and Beads/session documentation blocks.

Refactor the sync pipeline into smaller, composable components so contributors can maintain and extend it without scrolling through 1k+ lines. Split concerns into sourced libraries or scripts (argument parsing, detection, data preparation, renderers per target tool) while preserving the current CLI surface and behavior. Add regression coverage (ShellSpec/bats or script-driven tests) for the most common flows (Claude, Codex, multi-tool) and document the new structure so future work can hook into the right layer.

Ensure the refactor keeps existing functionality intact (hooks, Beads instructions, index generation, .claude/.codex outputs) while making the codebase manageable and testable.

title: Add slash command detection to centralized-rules hook for git and quality gates
description:
Enhanced the activate-rules.sh UserPromptSubmit hook to detect slash commands like /xgit, /xtest, /xsecurity, /xquality, etc. This ensures that when users invoke skills via slash commands (e.g., /xgit to commit and push), the centralized-rules system will automatically load relevant coding rules (git-workflow, testing-philosophy, security-principles, etc.) even though the prompt doesn't contain explicit keywords like 'commit' or 'test'.

Key Changes:
- Updated .claude/hooks/activate-rules.sh to detect slash commands via regex patterns
- Added slash command detection for: git (/xgit, /git, /xcommit, /commit, /push), testing (/xtest, /test, /xtdd), security (/xsecurity, /security, /xaudit), and refactoring (/xrefactor, /xquality, /xoptimize)
- Updated .claude/skills/skill-rules.json to document supported slash commands
- Created comprehensive test suite (tests/test-slash-command-detection.sh) with 16 passing tests
- All tests verify that slash commands correctly trigger their associated rule categories

Benefits:
- Users can invoke external skills like /xgit without explicitly mentioning 'commit' or 'push'
- Centralized-rules will still detect the intent and load appropriate quality gates
- Works with any skill that performs git, testing, security, or quality operations
- Provides consistency across different invocation methods (keywords vs slash commands)

title: Add Codex activation hook and installer support
description:
Goal: Provide an installation and activation path so Codex CLI/Desktop sessions automatically execute the centralized rules activation workflow before answering user prompts.

Scope / Required changes:
- Extend `install-hooks.sh` (or add a sibling script) with a `--tool codex` option that installs `.codex/hooks/activate-rules.sh`, copies shared libs into `.codex/lib/`, and updates the Codex settings file (document the path) so the hook runs on every prompt similar to Claude's `UserPromptSubmit` hook.
- Author a Codex-specific hook script that mirrors `.claude/hooks/activate-rules.sh`: detects languages/frameworks via `lib/detection.sh`, matches keywords/slash commands, then injects the "evaluate → apply → implement" banner along with instructions to load the relevant `.codex/rules/...` files.
- Update `.beads/keyword-expansion-roadmap.md` and related docs if new Codex-specific keywords or slash commands are required.
- Document assumptions/gaps if Codex lacks a direct hook API; provide fallback instructions (e.g., manual `/rules` command) and note any dependencies on Codex CLI versions.

Dependencies & Assumptions:
- Blocks on `centralized-rules-r27a` (Codex artifacts) and `centralized-rules-w6gf` (docs/templates) so the hook knows what to load and what to reference.
- Assumes Codex exposes a hook or configuration entry analogous to Claude's `UserPromptSubmit`; if not, this task must define the integration point and record the constraint.

title: Add Codex regression tests and verification docs
description:
Goal: Validate Codex parity end-to-end so we know the new `.codex/` artifacts, documentation, and hooks actually enforce centralized rules for Codex developers.

Scope / Required changes:
- Add automated tests (e.g., `scripts/test-codex-sync.sh`) that run `./sync-ai-rules.sh --tool codex` inside representative Python/TypeScript sample projects and assert the `.codex/rules/**` files, `index.json`, and `AGENTS.md` contain the correct sections.
- Create a smoke test (bash or node) that simulates the Codex hook invocation by piping JSON prompts through `.codex/hooks/activate-rules.sh` and verifying the injected instruction references `.codex/rules/...` and the Analyze → Load → Announce steps.
- Integrate these tests into CI (GitHub Actions and/or `scripts/verify-installation.sh`) so Codex support regresses if artifacts drift from the Claude implementation.
- Update developer docs with a "Verification" section describing how builders can rerun the Codex tests locally.

Dependencies & Assumptions:
- Depends on the previous Codex work (`centralized-rules-r27a`, `centralized-rules-w6gf`, `centralized-rules-8gjv`).
- Assumes access to Codex CLI for manual verification; automated tests will mock the hook interface if real Codex APIs are unavailable.

title: Display active tool in activation banners
description:
Goal: Make the activation banner explicitly announce which tool is currently enforcing centralized rules so builders immediately see “Claude Code” vs “Codex” context.

Scope / Required changes:
- Update `.claude/hooks/activate-rules.sh` (and the upcoming `.codex/hooks/activate-rules.sh`) to print a line such as `Tool: Claude Code CLI` / `Tool: Codex` at the top of the banner, alongside the repo/commit info, so users know which assistant was detected.
- Ensure the TypeScript hook (`skill/src/hooks/before-response.ts`) and any future Codex banner include the same tool identifier inside the `📋 Centralized Rules Active` block that gets injected into system prompts.
- Document the behavior in the hooks README / Codex integration doc so builders know where the tool name comes from and how to override it if needed (e.g., env var `CENTRALIZED_RULES_TOOL_NAME`).

Dependencies & Assumptions:
- Depends on `centralized-rules-8gjv` for the Codex hook path; Claude changes can ship immediately but banner parity waits for the Codex hook to exist.
- Assumes tool name can be inferred from the directory executing the hook (`.claude` vs `.codex`) or a config flag; call out any additional detection logic implemented.
